# Build with TypeSafe

TypeSafe makes units of AI intelligence usable like programming primitives: small
judgments you can compose into larger capabilities. Its **System One models** return
fast, focused judgments that software can consume directly. **Jev** is TypeSafe's
flagship and first System One model. It understands natural language and returns
typed answers and probabilities rather
than generating text or reasoning explanations. Code owns the workflow; the model
supplies programmable common sense where ordinary code needs semantic understanding.

## Read the live docs

**The live TypeSafe docs are the source of truth. Read them as part of the task.**
This skill gives direction; the docs carry current concepts, prompting guidance,
API contracts, SDK usage, models, limits, and worked examples.

- Start with the [documentation index](https://docs.typesafe.ai/llms.txt) to discover
  relevant pages and cookbooks. Use targeted reads rather than loading the entire site.
- Mintlify serves Markdown by appending `.md` to a page path, for example
  [how to build with TypeSafe](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md).
  Follow links from the index; convert extensionless documentation page links to
  `.md` when useful. Resolve relative links against `https://docs.typesafe.ai`.
- Before writing an integration, read the current API or chosen SDK page and the
  question guidance relevant to the design. For a new workflow, also inspect the
  closest cookbook: it often shows a better decomposition than a generic classifier.
- If the index is unavailable, use the direct links below or the site's navigation.
  If Markdown fetching fails, try the normal page. If live access is unavailable,
  use available local docs or installed SDK types, state that limitation, and avoid
  inventing version-dependent details.

| Task | Start here; follow the relevant details |
| --- | --- |
| Understand the programming model | [System One](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/system-one.md), [building guide](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/how-to-build-with-system-one.md) |
| Explore what to build | [Use-case map](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/use-case-map.md), then relevant cookbooks from the index |
| Prepare inputs and questions | [State](https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md), [primitives](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives.md), then the chosen primitive's page |
| Decide how to handle uncertainty | [Confidence](https://docs.typesafe.ai/confidence.md) |
| Write API code | [HTTP API](https://docs.typesafe.ai/api.md), [Python SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/python.md), or [JavaScript SDK](https://docs.typesafe.ai/sdk/javascript.md) |
| Update an older integration | [Migration guide](https://docs.typesafe.ai/migrating-to-v1.md) and the installed SDK's current reference |

## Find the useful shape

Start from the behavior the user wants: what will the application show, select,
change, or hand off? Work backward to the judgments it needs. Keep known rules,
calculations, exact lookups, and execution in code. Preserve the user's chosen stack
and scope; add TypeSafe where semantic understanding helps.

When brainstorming or choosing an architecture, consider more than classification.
The patterns below are starting points: combine primitives around the user's goal,
including ideas that do not fit an established recipe.

- **Route and fill known arguments.** A request can select a handler and its typed
  parameters. Ask useful branch-specific questions up front and consume only the
  relevant answers. Explore [function calling](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/function_calling.md)
  and [speculative fan-out](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/fan-out.md).
- **Select instead of generate.** Find candidate values or source spans in code,
  use a judgment to select the intended one, then copy or normalize it. Code can
  also assemble source text into a formatted document or reading guide. Explore
  [value extraction](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/pre_parsed_value_extraction_cookbook.md)
  and [structure recovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoformat.md).
- **Find and judge evidence.** Retrieve candidates, compare their relevance to a
  query, and select useful context. Explore [reranking](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/rerank_typesafe.md)
  and [hierarchical classification](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/hierarchical_classification.md).
- **Turn judgments into reusable data.** Score dimensions once, then let code or
  user controls change weights, thresholds, rankings, and views. With labeled
  outcomes, those signals can become classical ML features. Explore
  [composite scoring](https://docs.typesafe.ai/patterns/composite-scoring.md) and
  [feature discovery](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/autoresearch_feature_discovery.md).
- **Verify and escalate.** Check specific claims or fields against their evidence;
  send uncertain or failing cases to a person or reasoning model. Explore
  [citation checks](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/citation_check.md) and
  [extraction cascades](https://docs.typesafe.ai/cookbooks/sde_cascade.md).
- **Respond to changing state.** Code can retain goals and observations while fresh
  judgments guide the next bounded step. Keep inferred state distinct from observed
  facts, and check freshness before applying a result to a changed situation.

For open-ended requests, offer the few directions that best serve the user's goal
and recommend a starting point. For a concrete request, choose the relevant pattern
and build; a brainstorm is not a mandatory detour.

## Design the judgments

Choose by what the answer means, then read the relevant primitive page:

| Need | Primitive | Important distinction |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One of a defined set | [Choice](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/choice.md) | Picks one option; its distribution compares competing options |
| Whether a condition holds | [Noul](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul.md) | Probability of yes; no separate confidence; use one per label when several may apply |
| Degree along a described dimension | [Score](https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/score.md) | Probability-weighted position on ordered levels; use comparable per-item Scores for graded ranking |

Give each question enough relevant **state** to answer: source text, identities,
relationships, policies, and current facts. Prefer named JSON fields when context
has several parts. Put the judgment in **instructions** and define its possible
answers in **criteria**. Question IDs are for code and are not sent to the model;
include complete meaning in the question. Reference nested state with backticked
paths such as `ticket.messages[0].text`.

Ask one narrow, coherent judgment per question. Split independently useful dimensions,
without destroying the relationship being judged. A bounded action selection or
contextual interpretation is valid; atomic does not mean literal fact extraction
or a one-sentence limit. Strings work for simple questions. Use structured objects
or arrays when definitions, contrasts, exclusions, or examples clarify instructions
or criteria. Score levels must describe concrete situations and stand on their own.

Keep the needed answers available. Include a no-match outcome when nothing may fit;
use a separate presence judgment when it is independently useful. For source-value
selection, check candidate coverage: the model cannot choose an omitted value.

## Compose and verify

**Ask independent questions over the same state together**, including useful
speculative questions. They run in parallel and cannot see one another's answers.
State each speculative premise explicitly; code consumes the applicable answers.
A second request is warranted when an earlier answer is needed to fetch evidence,
construct new state, or determine the next options. Extra questions still use tokens;
measure actual request budgets, cost, and end-to-end latency.

Use probabilities and confidence to guide behavior, with thresholds evaluated on
the user's data and consequences. Choice/Score confidence summarizes distribution
concentration, not overall workflow correctness or permission to act. A Noul near
0.5 means similar probability for yes and no, not medium intensity. Several
acceptable alternatives can also spread probability; low confidence need not
invalidate a harmless preference choice. Ignore uncertainty on unused branches.

Keep policy explicit and raw judgments reusable. Weighted scores suit compensating
preferences; an “any serious violation” rule needs separate conditions. Changing a
weight or display filter need not rerun inference when evidence and question meanings
are unchanged. Typed output guarantees the interface, not truth. System One models
are trained for calibrated decisions; validate their performance in the target domain.

Test representative cases and the resulting application behavior. For failures,
inspect the exact state, questions, candidates, answers, composition, and observed
outcome. Separate missing evidence, model errors, code errors, and service failures.
Treat cookbook thresholds and demo results as examples to evaluate, not universal
rules or permanent model limitations. Keep API credentials server-side in web apps.

content.text:
**Could Jev help?** Yes, in one specific place: re-sorting search results. It's the most promising way to drop Docker without losing search by meaning.

- **The gap it would fill.** Plain keyword search misses questions worded differently from the note, such as "why the Soviet electrical muscle stimulation strength gains didn't replicate". That gap is currently the only reason to keep memsearch running in Docker.
- **How it would work.** Keyword search pulls the top 30 notes in about a millisecond. Jev then answers "does this note answer the question?" for each one, and the list is re-sorted by its answers. TypeSafe's own reranking example documents this pattern. In that example, getting the right answer into the top 10 went from 38% to 62%.
- **Cost.** About a fifth of a cent per search at their published price, and no Docker.
- **Speed.** One round of parallel calls to their cloud service. Their docs don't give a speed figure, so it has to be measured.
- **Catch 1, privacy.** The note text would go to TypeSafe's cloud. Your memory includes personal items like the dental plan, so certain folders would need to be kept out. DexaProject data is never in these folders.
- **Catch 2, accuracy on your notes is unproven.** Jev failed your Drive triage test at 76.5%. The search test we just built is how to find out before relying on it: add "keyword search + Jev" as a fourth method and score it on the same 30 questions.
- **Where Jev doesn't help: writing the test questions.** The right answer for each question should come from what the original session actually used, not from another model's judgment.

**Next item: nothing that changes the index before tonight.** Tonight's run is the first memsearch-with-vault score. If the index or its folders change now, that number can't be compared with today's baseline.

What can go ahead now, in my order of preference:
1. **Add the keyword search + Jev method to the test.** Tomorrow's results would then compare all four methods side by side. This is the change that could make the Docker decision.
2. **Clean up three leftover config entries the audit found:**
   - a `dcg` hook entry with a Mac path and no guard, in Windows settings;
   - an `ms-search` command that's referenced but doesn't exist here;
   - an old Codex memsearch hook that's still wired up.

   These are small and don't affect tonight's run.
3. **After tonight:** stop the project status/handoff docs from flooding results. They're 68% of the index and showed up in half the real-query results. Changing this now would skew tonight's comparison.

Should I do 1 and 2 now? For item 1, which folders should stay out of Jev? My default is to exclude `SecondBrain/Inbox/meetings` and the session transcripts, and send only the vault's book and knowledge notes, the compiled knowledge articles, and the project memory notes.

"""Prove the global TypeSafe API key resolves and the System One API answers.

There is deliberately no python-dotenv here. The key is meant to be available
globally from the environment (macOS Keychain -> ~/.zshenv -> every zsh), so
reading anything other than os.environ would hide a broken setup.

Run:  python smoke_test.py
"""

import os
import sys

REQUIRED_VAR = "TYPESAFE_API_KEY"


def require_key() -> None:
    if os.environ.get(REQUIRED_VAR):

"""Score memsearch against pre-registered recall questions. See docs/RERANK_MEASUREMENT.md.

    python rerank_measure/score.py rerank_measure/questions.json [--reranker MODEL]

A hit is a chunk, not a file: its source is one of the question's answer files AND
its text contains at least half of the answer keywords (case-insensitive). Coverage
is checked first, against the Milvus `source` field, so an answer that was never
indexed is reported as a coverage miss rather than a ranking miss.

Local only. memsearch embeds with an on-box ONNX model; nothing here calls TypeSafe.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from pymilvus import MilvusClient

K = 20


def norm(path: str) -> str:
    return path.replace("\\", "/").lower().rstrip("/")


def indexed_sources() -> set[str]:
    client = MilvusClient("http://localhost:19530")
    rows = client.query("memsearch_chunks", filter="", output_fields=["source"], limit=16384)
    return {norm(r["source"]) for r in rows}


def search(question: str, reranker: str | None) -> list[dict]:
    cmd = ["memsearch", "search", question, "-k", str(K), "-j"]
    if reranker is not None:
        cmd += ["--reranker-model", reranker]
    out = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True, encoding="utf-8", check=True)
    return json.loads(out.stdout)


def is_hit(chunk: dict, answer_files: set[str], keywords: list[str]) -> bool:
    if norm(chunk.get("source", "")) not in answer_files:
        return False
    text = (chunk.get("content") or chunk.get("text") or "").lower()
    found = sum(1 for k in keywords if k.lower() in text)
    return found * 2 >= len(keywords)


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("questions")
    parser.add_argument("--reranker", default=None)
    args = parser.parse_args()

    questions = json.loads(Path(args.questions).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    sources = indexed_sources()
    rows = []
    for q in questions:
        files = {norm(f) for f in q["answer_files"]}
        covered = bool(files & sources)
        rank = None
        if covered:
            for i, chunk in enumerate(search(q["question"], args.reranker), start=1):
                if is_hit(chunk, files, q["answer_keywords"]):
                    rank = i
                    break
        rows.append({"id": q["id"], "covered": covered, "rank": rank,
                     "question": q["question"][:70]})

    for r in rows:
        where = "NOT INDEXED" if not r["covered"] else (f"rank {r['rank']}" if r["rank"] else f"miss@{K}")
        print(f"{r['id']:>4}  {where:<12} {r['question']}")
    hit5 = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"] and r["rank"] <= 5)
    hit20 = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"])
    band = sum(1 for r in rows if r["rank"] and r["rank"] > 5)
    uncovered = sum(1 for r in rows if not r["covered"])
    print(f"\nhit@5 {hit5}/{len(rows)}   hit@{K} {hit20}/{len(rows)}   "
          f"ranks 6-{K} {band}   not indexed {uncovered}")
    json.dump(rows, sys.stderr)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recall eval: can each retrieval backend find the known answer file?

Runs every case in questions.jsonl against up to three backends over the SAME
roots (KeystoneOS data/memory-index-paths.json, tokens resolved per machine):

  memsearch  vector search (Milvus + ONNX embedder), top 5 distinct files
  fts5       stdlib SQLite FTS5 / BM25 over whole files, natural-language query
  rg         ripgrep on the case's `keyword`, files ranked by match count

Per case: rank of the first expected file, latency, failure, and coverage
(does an expected file exist under the configured roots on THIS machine --
the check that exposes path drift like the 2026-09-30 {VAULT} bug).

Writes results/<date>-<machine>-<label>.json and appends one row per backend
to ledger.md. Stdlib only. Spec: ../2026-09-30-memory-infra-audit.md section 6.

  python recall-eval.py --label opus-5.5            # all backends
  python recall-eval.py --backends fts5,rg          # skip memsearch (no Docker / low RAM)
"""
import argparse, datetime, json, os, platform, re, shutil, sqlite3, statistics, subprocess, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
HOME = Path.home()


def first_dir(cands, marker=None):
    for c in cands:
        if (c / marker if marker else c).is_dir():

JEV_ALLOWED = ("/secondbrain/knowledge/", "/claude-memory-compiler/knowledge/", "/.claude/projects/")
JEV_POOL = 30
JEV_CHARS = 2000
JEV_URL = "https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone"
_JEV_KEY = None

def jev_allowed(path):
    n = norm(path)
    return any(a in n for a in JEV_ALLOWED) and "/memory/" in n if "/.claude/projects/" in n else any(a in n for a in JEV_ALLOWED)


def jev_key():
    global _JEV_KEY
    if _JEV_KEY is None:
        _JEV_KEY = os.environ.get("TYPESAFE_API_KEY", "")
        env = HOME / ".claude" / "typesafe.env"
        if not _JEV_KEY and env.exists():
            for line in env.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
                if line.startswith("TYPESAFE_API_KEY="):
                    _JEV_KEY = line.split("=", 1)[1].strip().strip("'\\"")
        if not _JEV_KEY:
            raise RuntimeError("no TYPESAFE_API_KEY")
    return _JEV_KEY


def jev_answers(query, path):
    text = Path(path).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")[:JEV_CHARS]
    body = {"model": "jev-latest",
            "state": {"query": query, "note": {"title": Path(path).stem, "text": text}},
            "questions": {"answers": {"type": "noul",

                                      "criteria": {"yes": "The note directly addresses what the query asks about.",
                                                   "no": "The note is about something else or only mentions the words in passing."}}}}
    req = urllib.request.Request(JEV_URL, data=json.dumps(body).encode(),
                                 headers={"Authorization": "Bearer " + jev_key(), "Content-Type": "application/json"})
    for attempt in range(5):
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=60) as r:
                out = json.loads(r.read())
            JEV_USAGE["calls"] += 1
            JEV_USAGE["input_tokens"] += out.get("usage", {}).get("input_tokens", 0)
            return out["answers"]["answers"]["noul"]
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as e:
            if e.code in (429, 529) and attempt < 4:
                time.sleep(2 ** attempt)
                continue
            raise RuntimeError(f"TypeSafe HTTP {e.code}: {e.read()[:120]!r}")


def b_jev(q, case):

    case["_jev_pool_hit"] = rank_of(pool, case["expected"])
    return out[:5]

content.text: I'm giving the Codex hook the same 30-minute cooldown the Claude hook has. They share one "last run" file, so a Codex turn won't start an index minutes after a Claude session already did:

input.new_string:
$memsearch = Get-Command memsearch -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    if (-not $memsearch) { exit 0 }

    # Codex fires Stop after EVERY turn, so without this a busy session started a
    # 45s index each turn. Share the Claude hook's cooldown file (memsearch-sync.js,
    # 30 min, mtime-based) so the two harnesses start at most one index per window.
    $lastRunFile = Join-Path $transcriptsDir ".memsearch-last-run"
    $cooldownMin = 30
    if ((Test-Path -LiteralPath $lastRunFile) -and
        ((Get-Date) - (Get-Item -LiteralPath $lastRunFile).LastWriteTime).TotalMinutes -lt $cooldownMin) { exit 0 }

input.content:
# Unattended follow-up to a scheduled reindex + recall eval (Task Scheduler, \Eric\memsearch-drain-*).
# Runs as the last action of the task, after memsearch-drain.ps1 and recall-eval.py:
#   1. checks the index finished (memsearch-drain.log ends in exit=0),
#   2. checks recall-eval wrote ledger rows in the last 24 h,
#   3. commits + pushes the ledger and results in ~/.claude (nothing else on Windows does),
#   4. writes LATEST.md here with the rows,
#   5. ONLY on a problem, appends one line to .errors.log, which every session surfaces
#      at startup (same pattern as claude-stack-doctor/weekly-check.ps1).
param([string]$Label = '')

$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$here = $PSScriptRoot
$claude = Join-Path $HOME '.claude'
$errLog = Join-Path $claude 'global-memory\transcripts\.errors.log'
$problems = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()

$drainLog = Join-Path $claude 'scripts\logs\memsearch-drain.log'
$drainLast = if (Test-Path $drainLog) { Get-Content $drainLog -Tail 1 } else { '' }
$indexOk = $drainLast -match 'exit=0'
if (-not $indexOk) { $problems.Add("index did not finish cleanly (last drain line: '$drainLast')") }

$ledger = Join-Path $here 'ledger.md'
$since = (Get-Date).AddHours(-24).ToString('yyyy-MM-dd')
$rows = @()
if (Test-Path $ledger) {
    $rows = @(Get-Content $ledger | Where-Object { $_ -match '^\| (\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) ' -and $Matches[1] -ge $since -and (-not $Label -or $_ -match [regex]::Escape("| $Label"))})
}
if ($rows.Count -eq 0) { $problems.Add("recall-eval wrote no ledger rows$(if ($Label) { " labelled '$Label'" }) in the last 24 h") }

$git = 'C:\Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe'
$pushed = $false
if ($rows.Count -gt 0) {
    & $git -C $claude add -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
    & $git -C $claude diff --cached --quiet -- audits/recall-eval
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        & $git -C $claude commit -q -m "recall-eval: scheduled run $(Get-Date -Format yyyy-MM-dd) $Label" -- audits/recall-eval/ledger.md audits/recall-eval/results 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude pull -q --no-rebase --no-edit 2>&1 | Out-Null
        & $git -C $claude push -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
        $pushed = $LASTEXITCODE -eq 0
        if (-not $pushed) { $problems.Add('commit made but git push failed (run git pull/push in ~/.claude)') }
    } else { $pushed = $true }
}

$status = if ($problems.Count) { 'PROBLEM: ' + ($problems -join '; ') } else { 'OK' }
@(
    "# Latest scheduled recall eval"
    ""
    "Run finished $(Get-Date -Format 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm') on $env:COMPUTERNAME. Status: $status"
    "Index: $drainLast"
    ""
    "| date | machine | label | backend | n | hit@1 | hit@5 | MRR | p50 ms | p95 ms | fail% | coverage% | by layer (hit@5) |"
    "|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|"
) + $rows | Set-Content -LiteralPath (Join-Path $here 'LATEST.md') -Encoding utf8

if ($problems.Count) {
    Add-Content -LiteralPath $errLog -Encoding utf8 -Value "[$(Get-Date -Format o)] recall-eval scheduled run: $($problems -join '; ') - see ~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/LATEST.md"
}
exit 0

Durable schedule and capability facts for the Mac automation stack. These are stable
settings, not active threads — health-check them with `/claude-stack-doctor`.

## Ritual nudges (launchd `com.keystone.rituals`)

- **Weekdays 17:00** → `/interview-me`
- **Fridays 15:30** → `/weekly-review`
- `harvest` and `forecast-capture` also run through `ritual-check.ps1`; their
  due/overdue state is computed from their own output, not from a fixed clock
  (forecast-capture is Monday-anchored and season-bounded — see
  [[cfb-forecast-capture]]). Four rituals total; `Name    = ` in
  `KeystoneOS/scripts/ritual-check.ps1` is the authoritative list.

The nudge is only a prompt; **the output artifact is the record**, not the reminder firing.

## memsearch reindex

Reindex **rides the daily backup task** rather than running on its own timer. The
nightly moved 00:30 → **09:00 on 2026-08-29** (CRASHBOX was unplugged at 00:30), so
any reasoning that assumes an overnight reindex is wrong — the backup's uncapped full reindex absorbs backlogs the
short SessionEnd hook can't finish. See [[backup-sync-system]].

## OS audits

Full OS audit last run **2026-07-24** (reports under `audits/`, guards auto-run);
**next due 2026-10-24**.

## Capability limits worth remembering

- **gws `invalid_client: The provided client secret is invalid` = stale client SECRET, not
  token rot** — re-auth alone never fixes it. The secret for client `208643585660-3ogm…`
  (project `baylor-gws`) was rotated 2026-09-17 to one ending `Xyjf`; the Mac kept the
  June one until 2026-09-30, when the Windows copy was carried over via Drive. Console no
  longer shows or downloads a secret: copy the other machine's `client_secret.json`, or
  Add secret (shown once). Then login, then delete `token_cache.json`.
- **gws** re-auth requires explicit full scope URLs — the `-s drive`
  shorthand silently grants no scopes (v0.22.5 bug), and `~/.config/gws/token_cache.json`
  must be deleted after re-auth or the stale token is served. See [[gws-forms-api]].
- **MCP Gmail is draft-only** — it can compose drafts but must not be treated as a send path.

## reMarkable OCR

`remarkable_extract.py` — USB-first with a `--cloud` fallback; Vision API key lives in
`.env`.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\memory-write

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

content.text:
Mostly no, and the reason isn't Task Scheduler.

- **Docker is the blocker.** memsearch needs Milvus, which runs inside Docker Desktop. Docker Desktop is a desktop app that only runs while you're signed in, so the memsearch step would fail after sign-out whatever the task settings say.
- **The commit and push would fail too.** Git uses your saved GitHub login from Windows Credential Manager. A task that runs while you're signed out can't reach it unless it stores your Baylor password. That breaks every time the password changes, and Baylor's policy may block it anyway.
- **What would work signed out:** keyword search, ripgrep and keyword search + Jev. But the memsearch number is the whole point of tonight's run.

**Locking the screen is enough.** Press Win+L instead of signing out: your session stays signed in and both tasks run normally. Tonight's task can also wake the laptop from sleep.

The one thing that would still break it is a forced overnight restart for Windows updates, which signs you out. If Baylor pushes those, check that no restart is pending before you leave.

content.text:
Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\eric_rash\.claude\skills\closeout

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). It copies every repo's `docs/*.md` into `~/.claude/global-memory/dev-docs/`, which is on the index list. One line of output; do this after Step 4 so today's STATUS is included.
- If this session produced a durable decision or new active thread, update `~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (respect the 2,500-char cap; consolidate before adding) or write a Tier A memory file per the memory-system rules in CLAUDE.md.
- **Tier A does not cross machines — mirror it or lose it.** Project memory lives under a slug built from the project's absolute path, and that path differs on the Mac and the Windows laptop, so a Tier A file written today is not auto-injected tomorrow on the other machine. Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

## Step 4 — Cross-harness handoff

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)
- Exact file paths of everything created or modified this session
- Next actions, most important first
- Anything mid-flight (open questions, awaited inputs)

Plain markdown, no harness-specific syntax — Codex, Antigravity, or a fresh Claude session must be able to resume from it. Commit it with the Step 2 commit when in a repo.

**Always, in every repo touched (even for light sessions): update `docs/STATUS.md`.** It is the file the next session reads first, on either machine, in any harness. Rewrite the sections in place, keep it short:

- `## Current state` — two to five lines on where things stand today
- `## Next` — most important first
- `## Open questions` — decisions waiting on Eric
- `## Gotchas` — anything that will bite the next session

The dated handoff file is the detailed record; STATUS.md is the summary. Do Step 4 before the Step 2 commit so both land in the same push.

## Step 5 — Verdict

End with a single short report:

```
## Closeout — <date>

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
**Memory:** captured ✓ / issue found: <what> / skipped (Cowork, no hooks)
**Handoff:** <path, or "not needed — no substantive work">
**Still open:** <numbered list, or "none">

Clear to sign off. / Not clear: <the one thing blocking>.
```

"Clear to sign off" means: every touched repo is pushed (or is a declared local-only repo). If anything is unpushed, the verdict is "Not clear" and the unpushed repo is the one thing blocking.

Every file created or modified during the session must appear somewhere in the report with its full path — "where did this save?" should never need to be asked.

## Rules

- Push every touched DEV repo. Do not leave the laptop with unpushed work; the other machine pulls from GitHub, not from this disk.
- Never skip Step 3 — memory capture failing silently is the user's top recurring worry.
- If a check fails and the fix is quick and safe (restage a file, clear a stale lock), fix it and note it. If the fix is risky, list it under "Still open" instead.
- Total output should fit on one screen. The user is leaving; brevity is the deliverable.

# Handoff 2026-09-30 — memory/infra audit, vault index fix, recall eval

Windows laptop session. Question: with Claude 5-era models, is memsearch's Docker/Milvus
still worth running, and how do we audit the memory stack repeatably?

## What happened

1. A Fable subagent audited the stack read-only:
   `~/.claude/audits/2026-09-30-memory-infra-audit.md`. Verdict: retire Docker/Milvus on
   Windows eventually (it exists only because milvus-lite has no Windows wheel; ~1.7 GB RAM),
   but first fix coverage: the SecondBrain vault had **never been indexed on Windows**.
2. Vault fix: `KeystoneOS/data/memory-index-paths.json` now uses a `{VAULT}` token
   (~/SecondBrain on Mac, ~/Desktop/SecondBrain on Windows) and also lists the Windows
   workspace Tier A folder. Every reader resolves it: `~/.claude/hooks/memsearch-sync.js`
   (also logs skipped roots in `.memsearch-index.log`), `~/.claude/scripts/daily-backup.ps1`
   (also: `$DevRoot` resolves per machine), `~/.claude/scripts/memsearch-drain.ps1`,
   `KeystoneOS/scripts/codex-hooks/memsearch-sync.ps1` (also gains `{DEV}` and the shared
   30-min cooldown). KeystoneOS test updated.
3. Recall eval built: `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/` — `questions.jsonl` (30 known-answer
   cases), `recall-eval.py` (backends memsearch / fts5 / rg / jev), `ledger.md`, `results/`,
   `after-run.ps1` (commit+push results, write `LATEST.md`, alert `.errors.log` only on a
   problem). Wired into claude-stack-doctor (`recall-coverage`, `recall-regress`).
4. Jev (TypeSafe) backend: reranks fts5's top 30. Only vault `Knowledge/`, compiled
   knowledge, and Tier A project notes (not `user_*`) are ever sent; transcripts, dailies,
   meetings, briefings, dev-docs, Codex memories stay local (Eric's choice).
5. Config: removed the unguarded Mac-path `dcg` PreToolUse entry from `~/.claude/settings.json`
   (the guarded entry remains). `ms-search` was already gone from all skill copies.

## Numbers (n=30, vault included, memsearch not yet re-indexed)

| backend | hit@5 | hit@1 | p50 |
|---|---|---|---|
| fts5 | 25/30 | 21 | 1 ms |
| fts5+jev | 27/30 | 19 | 0.4 s (~$0.0175 per full run) |
| rg | 22/30 | 12 | 94 ms |

## Decisions and why

- Fix coverage before touching the backend: half of real queries had their answers in the
  unindexed vault; no backend fixes that.
- Don't change the index before tonight's run, so memsearch-with-vault is comparable.
- Decision rule (audit §6.2): retire the heavier layer when the cheaper one is within 1 hit@5
  on n≥30 for two consecutive runs.
- A first index attempt this afternoon was killed for low RAM (0.7 GB free; ~18 Claude
  processes); reindex moved overnight.

## Scheduled

- `\Eric\memsearch-drain-once` — 2026-09-30 22:30: reindex → eval (4 backends, label
  `post-vault-index`) → after-run.ps1. Needs Eric logged in (lock, don't sign out): Docker
  Desktop only runs in a signed-in session.
- `\Eric\memsearch-drain-weekly` — Sundays 02:00, same chain, label `weekly`.

## Next

1. Morning: `~/.claude/audits/recall-eval/LATEST.md` (status line + four rows). No recall-eval
   line in startup errors = it went through.
2. If fts5+jev ≥ memsearch again on Sunday's run, retire Docker/Milvus on Windows (audit §5.3
   steps, §5.4 rollback).
3. After that: demote dev-docs in the index (68% of it; pollutes results) — audit §7 #4.
4. Mac: `git pull` in `~/.claude`, `~/.claude/skills`, `~/DEV/KeystoneOS` before its 21:00 backup.

## Open

- Should `SecondBrain/Knowledge/career-strategy/` and `faith/` also be excluded from Jev?
  Currently sent (covered by the approved default).
- Until the vault backlog clears, SessionEnd index attempts may time out (up to 6 before
  `.errors.log` alerts) — expected.
